questions.question: What is the definition of climate?
options: The daily changes in wind speed and rainfall in a specific town
The atmospheric conditions recorded at a single moment in time
The average weather conditions for a particular location over a long period of time
The seasonal variation in temperature from one month to the next

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary cause of modern global warming and climate change?
options: Natural changes in the Earth's orbit around the Sun
Emissions of greenhouse gases from human activities
Shifts in the magnetic field of the Earth
Heat released from deep-ocean volcanic eruptions

questions.question: How does climate change affect the occurrence of extreme weather events like droughts, storms, and floods?
options: It causes an increase in their frequency
It leads to a complete elimination of these events
It has no measurable effect on how often they happen
It decreases their frequency while making them last longer

questions.question: What is required of global communities to successfully limit climate change?
options: Relying solely on natural ecosystems to absorb all emissions
We all need to work together to reduce greenhouse gas emissions
Moving all agricultural production indoors
Stopping all scientific research into alternative energy sources

questions.question: Which of the following stages of food production contributes to its overall carbon footprint?
options: Only the transportation of food from farms to shops
Only the packaging used to display the food in retail stores
Land-use change, farming, processing, transport, retail, and packaging
Only the chemical processing that happens in food factories

questions.question: When comparing meat and plant-based food products, what is a key difference regarding their environmental impact?
options: They have identical carbon footprints regardless of how they are produced
Meat and plant-based products have different carbon footprints
Plant-based products always have a higher carbon footprint than meat
Neither meat nor plant-based products contribute to carbon emissions

questions.question: How can individuals alter their daily habits to help eat more sustainably and lower greenhouse gas emissions?
options: By increasing food waste and eating more processed meats
By purchasing only imported foods wrapped in heavy plastic
By making changes in diet and reducing food waste
By consuming larger portions of food than necessary

questions.question: What do temperature data from the last century or so reveal about the Earth's average surface temperature?
options: It has remained completely stable with no notable fluctuations
It shows an unusual, rapid increase
It shows a steady, gradual decline towards a new ice age
It has fluctuated wildly up and down with no overall trend

questions.question: What relationship is observed when comparing historical temperature data with data on greenhouse gas emissions?
options: There is a correlation showing that as greenhouse gas emissions increase, temperature also increases
There is an inverse relationship where higher emissions correspond to lower temperatures
There is no correlation or patterns observable between the two datasets
The two datasets show completely opposite trends in different hemispheres

questions.question: How do thermal insulators help make buildings more energy-efficient?
options: They generate extra heat energy when the building gets too cold
They reduce the energy needed to heat a building
They convert solar energy directly into electricity
They eliminate the need for any ventilation systems inside the house

questions.question: What is the function of thermostats in a household heating system?
options: They increase the rate of heat loss through the windows
They generate electricity using waste heat from appliances
They can control temperature automatically in different rooms and help reduce unnecessary heating
They automatically switch the home's energy source from fossil fuels to solar power

questions.question: Why do renewable resources not run out?
options: Because they are completely synthetic and made in laboratories
Because they are replenished faster than they are used up
Because humans have an infinite supply of them stored underground
Because their physical properties prevent them from being degraded

questions.question: Under what condition is wood considered a renewable resource?
options: Wood is always renewable, regardless of how quickly forests are cleared
Wood is only renewable if it is used sustainably
Wood is only renewable if it is imported from tropical regions
Wood is never renewable because trees take hundreds of years to grow

questions.question: Why is it impossible to have a sustainable transport system that relies on petrol or diesel fuel?
options: Petrol and diesel fuels are extremely expensive to refine
Engines using these fuels cannot travel long distances
We cannot have sustainable transport that uses petrol or diesel fuel
These fuels cause too much friction on road surfaces

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of the Earth's natural greenhouse effect?
options: It prevents all UV radiation from reaching the surface of the planet
A natural greenhouse effect maintains optimal temperature range for life on Earth
It keeps the oceans from rising above sea level
It stops the atmosphere from escaping into outer space

questions.question: Why are waste disposal methods like landfill sites and incinerators environmental concerns regarding climate change?
options: They absorb too much solar radiation, heating up the local ground
They are sources of greenhouse gases
They prevent rainwater from returning to the natural water cycle
They destroy the ozone layer directly through mechanical friction

questions.question: What is the recommended approach to minimise waste and its impact on the environment?
options: Burn all domestic waste in open fires
Bury all waste deep underground in sealed containers
Reuse, reduce, recycle is what we can do to minimise waste
Ship all waste to other countries for disposal
